To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inequality and mobility are negatively correlated and that the inequality decreases as the accounting period increases.

the inequality of lifetime incomes, measured by the Gini coefficient, is lower than that of annual incomes; and that the inequality of annual incomes is lower in a society with high income mobility than in a society with low mobility.

1) The income mobility index (IMI) is the ratio of the difference between inequality values for two different income accounting periods to the inequality value for the shorter accounting period; 2) IMI values are inversely related to inequality; 3) IMI values increase as the accounting period increases; 4) The IMI is a valid measure of the extent to which a society is income mobile.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a methodological question: can the relationship between mobility and equality be used as a basis for defining mobility?
the measurement of income mobility and the relationship between income mobility and inequality.

the development of measures of inequality and mobility, with particular attention to the relationship between them, and to the effects on the measurement of inequality of extending the accounting period over which income is measured.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Gini is a good measure of inequality and the Gini is also a good measure of mobility.
the Gini index of income inequality is an appropriate index of income inequality.
the mobility measure derived is a valid measure for mobility and inequality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to develop a new index of mobility for the study of income inequality.
we have developed a method of measuring the degree of mobility of a population over time.
we have developed an index of mobility based on the Gini index of inequality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mobility index is a good measure of the extent to which income mobility reduces income inequality.
the income mobility is not the complement of the income inequality and vice versa.
the inequality measure of income is more sensitive to mobility than the Gini index and that the inequality measure is more sensitive to income mobility than the Theil index.
